## Purpose

`liminal2` estimates how well a predictive modelling goal is adjudicated. The
canonical model combines six components with a weighted geometric mean:

\[
A(g) = \prod_{k=1}^{6} a_k(g)^{w_k}, \qquad L(g) = 1 - A(g).
\]

The six components are:

| Component | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `a1` | Label determinacy: agreement between rival target definitions |
| `a2` | Construct stability: temporal drift between adjacent time folds |
| `a3` | Predictive multiplicity: Rashomon-set ambiguity on holdout data |
| `a4` | Attainable discriminability: repeated cross-validated AUC |
| `a5` | Oracle strength: elicited quality of the adjudication oracle |
| `a6` | Normative consensus: elicited agreement on the target |

## A quick assessment

The package ships five benchmark scenarios. This example uses the
counterfactual long-run LTV scenario, which has high liminality.

```{r assessment}
library(liminal2)

scenario <- generate_scenario("S5", seed = 42)
goal <- assess_goal(
  label_defs = scenario$label_defs,
  X = scenario$X,
  time_index = scenario$time_index,
  y = scenario$y,
  oracle_scores = scenario$rubric$oracle,
  normative_scores = scenario$rubric$normative,
  component_args = list(
    a3 = list(variant = "subsample", B = 10),
    a4 = list(repeats = 2)
  ),
  seed = 42
)
goal
```

The assessment stores the component values, weights, dimensions and
provenance. It can be converted to a data frame or summarised.

```{r summary}
summary(goal)
as.data.frame(goal)
```

## Uncertainty and weight sensitivity

Bootstrap uncertainty resamples units for `a1` to `a4` and perturbs expert
scores for `a5` and `a6`.

```{r uncertainty}
boot <- bootstrap_liminality(goal, B = 10, seed = 42)
boot
```

Weight sensitivity draws weights from a Dirichlet distribution over the
component simplex.

```{r sensitivity}
weight_sensitivity(goal, n = 200, seed = 42)
```

## Dimensions

The components are grouped into epistemic, structural and normative
dimensions. The dominance rule reports the dimension with the largest
liminality and flags goals whose normative dimension both dominates and
exceeds 0.5.

```{r dimensions}
liminality_dimensions(goal$components)
liminal_case("causal_counterfactual")
```

## Measurement notes and design decisions

* `a5` and `a6` are supplied as anchored rubric score vectors. The package
  validates the anchors and does not ship an interactive scorer.
* Scenario S5 has a counterfactual target, so its `a4` value is a documented
  proxy over observed outcomes. The scenario truth records this as
  `identifiability = "proxy"`.
* Under the binary majority-vote definition, Rashomon ambiguity is at most
  0.5, so `a3` has a floor of 0.5. The authored S4 and S5 `a3` targets are
  below this floor; the benchmark acceptance criteria are stated in terms of
  the composite `L`.
* The estimators use base R. Suggested packages are used only for tests,
  cross-checks and development.

## Benchmark scenarios

```{r registry}
scenario_registry()[, c("id", "title", "target_A", "target_L")]
```

The benchmark script in `bench/run_benchmark.R` reproduces the five-scenario
acceptance test and writes `bench/results.csv`.
